chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa from Mansur from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The ending of the childhood of the orphan is the seminal emission (al-ihlam), and that is its most significant sign. If he emits semen but maturity (rushd) is not anticipated from him, and he is a fool or weak, then his guardian should retain his property.

key_terms.سَفِيهاً: fool or one lacking financial prudence

ai.seo_question: When does an orphan's childhood end and when does the guardian retain his property?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the legal transition from childhood to adulthood, establishing seminal emission (ihlam) as the primary biological marker for orphans. Crucially, the hadith distinguishes between physical maturity and intellectual capacity (rushd), ensuring that guardians retain control over the orphan's wealth if the youth is deemed 'safiha' (foolish or imprudent) to prevent financial mismanagement.
